title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Low vs. Medium vs. High effort
subtitle: All three passed 7/7. Cost fell 59% from High ($7.16) to Low ($2.97).
description: 7-slide 3-tier effort study of Gemini 4 Carbon (Low, Medium, High) on Antigravity CLI: U-shaped turn counts (122 → 97 → 198), zero thinking tokens on Low ($2.97, 54m), and 50 ms cold-boot Ctrl-C hardening.
seoTitle: Gemini 4 Carbon: Low vs Medium vs High Effort
seoDescription: Gemini 4 Carbon Low ($2.97, 54m, 122 turns), Medium ($3.35, 53m, 97 turns), and High ($7.16, 88m, 198 turns) all pass 7/7 on Antigravity CLI.

slides.label: COVER
slides.headlinePrimary: Gemini 4 Carbon: Low vs. Medium vs. High.
slides.headlineMuted: All three hit 7/7. Cost fell 59% from High to Low.

slides.label: U-SHAPED TURNS VS COST
slides.headlinePrimary: Medium took the fewest turns. Low won on cost.
slides.headlineMuted: Zero thinking tokens cut Low's output bill in half.

splitBar.label: Output Tokens: Low (77.2k, 0 thinking) vs Medium (150.1k, 62.4k thinking)

slides.label: LOW VS MEDIUM VS HIGH
slides.headlinePrimary: Low is now the cheapest Gemini 4 run at $2.97.
slides.headlineMuted: 11% cheaper than Medium and 59% cheaper than High.
slides.footnote: * Carbon Low ($2.97) is the only Gemini 4 run under $3.00 (ahead of Carbon Med $3.35, Argon $3.37, Hydrogen $3.42, Neon $3.69).

slides.label: CODE & SIGNAL DIFF
slides.headlinePrimary: How each tier handled HTTP and 50 ms Ctrl-C.
slides.headlineMuted: Three effort levels, three signal designs.

steps.title: Low: Mint.HTTP + SIGUSR2/SIGUSR1 handshake
steps.desc: Used offline `Mint.HTTP` (`584` LoC, `29/29` tests) and added a `CB_LAUNCHER_PID` `SIGUSR2`/`SIGUSR1` handshake (`b9a133a`) for `50 ms` cold-boot `Ctrl-C`.

steps.title: Medium: raw :gen_tcp/:ssl + post-boot trap
steps.desc: Built a zero-dependency `:gen_tcp`/`:ssl` client (`36/36` tests in `8` release turns), passing post-boot `Ctrl-C` (`>=350 ms`).

steps.title: High: raw :gen_tcp/:ssl + two-file handshake
steps.desc: Built raw `:gen_tcp`/`:ssl` (`42/42` tests) and spent `26` release turns adding a `CB_INTR_FILE` + `CB_READY_FILE` boot handshake.

callout.title: Low Solved the 50 ms Race Without Files
callout.body: When `Ctrl-C` arrives during BEAM boot, `./cb` latches `interrupted=1` until `SignalHandler` sends `kill -USR2 $CB_LAUNCHER_PID`.

slides.label: SMALL VS LARGE MODELS
slides.headlinePrimary: Small models fail on Low. Frontier models don't.
slides.headlineMuted: GLM-5.3-Flash vs Gemini 4 Carbon at Low effort.

steps.title: GLM-5.3-Flash Low (6/7 — spiraled)
steps.desc: At Low effort, the small Flash model looped for `344` turns (`$1.10`, `111m`) and failed live chunked `301` responses.

steps.title: Gemini 4 Carbon Low (7/7 — $2.97)
steps.desc: Even with `0` thinking tokens, Carbon passed all `7/7` stages in `54m` (`122` turns) and fixed its own `50 ms` cold-boot `Ctrl-C` race.

steps.title: Gemini 4 Carbon Medium (7/7 — 97 turns)
steps.desc: Adding `62.4k` thinking tokens cut turns to `97` (`11.12M` tokens, `53m`), trading `+$0.38` in output cost for `20%` fewer turns.

callout.title: Set Effort by Model Size
callout.body: Use **High** on small models to prevent spiral loops. Use **Low** or **Medium** on large models to avoid over-paying.

items.head: Why Low took 25 more turns than Medium
items.text: With `0` thinking tokens, Low spent extra turns inspecting local Hex tarballs in `S3` and iterating from `CB_READY_FILE` to `SIGUSR2` in release checks.

items.head: 300 ms cold-boot gap on Medium only
items.text: Both **Low** (`SIGUSR2`/`SIGUSR1` PID handshake) and **High** (`CB_READY_FILE`) print partial summaries on `50 ms` `Ctrl-C`; **Medium** needs `>=350 ms`.

items.head: Cache resets added $0.86 to High
items.text: High had `5` mid-run cache resets (`94.68%` hit) after a `19m57s` stream stall; Low (`96.43%`) and Medium (`96.39%`) had zero stalls.

items.head: 99%–100% file-edit accuracy across all 3 tiers
items.text: Low (`110/111`), Medium (`108/109`), and High (`99/99`) rarely missed an edit; `17–20` tool errors per run were deliberate red-phase TDD `mix test` runs.

slides.label: TAKEAWAYS
slides.headlineMuted: When to use Low, Medium, or High.

items.head: Use Low ($2.97) for lowest cost
items.text: Zero thinking tokens cut output billing by `49%` while clearing `7/7` in `54m` — including `50 ms` cold-boot `Ctrl-C` hardening.

items.head: Use Medium ($3.35) for fewest turns
items.text: Medium's `643` thinking tokens/turn and `2.01×` tool batching hit the turn minimum (`97` turns, `11.12M` tokens, `53m`).

items.head: Skip High ($7.16) on standard tasks
items.text: High doubled turns (`198`) and cost (`2.4×` Low) via single-tool micro-stepping (`1.17` tools/turn) without improving the `7/7` score.
